name: Zane Zhang

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, parties or government, and we sell nothing. Your answers are confidential. What does a normal day at work look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 27, have a bachelor’s degree and lead four small-business renewal clerks at an insurer. I earn above the typical rate because I catch gaps between a shop’s stock declaration and its policy; I use AI now and then to outline long letters but check the signed schedule myself. My wife Hana works in a school office, we have no children and we pay a mortgage together. We have ten months of expenses saved and plenty of nearby insurers, though I also like learning practical work from my family.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say a small filing tool could help our small-business policy desk, but a café owner still needs a clerk to explain a changed premium. I use AI now and then to outline long policy letters, then read the signed schedule myself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I lead four renewal clerks and earn a higher wage for spotting gaps between a business declaration and its actual stock. My wife Hana earns a current school-office wage, and our ten-month reserve makes our mortgage comfortable while both incomes hold.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep my Friday review of disputed business renewals and pay 100 extra toward the mortgage each month while both wages continue. In the first year I would use the same occasional letter outline and compare every changed premium against the signed policy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about this year’s work and house payment. A café can be busy and still have the wrong stock value on its policy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which business value went wrong?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A bakery listed old freezer stock after buying a larger unit. I called the owner before the renewal letter, and the declared value changed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you show a junior?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask a junior clerk to read the owner’s stock list, then show the signed schedule. Guessing from the last premium is the mistake.

say: I would check **stock declarations** before business renewals go out.
I would use **AI letter outlines occasionally** and verify signed terms.
think: I have **ten months saved** alongside two present wages.
I know **changed stock values** need a human question.
do: **Review disputed renewals** every Friday against stock declarations.
**Pay 100 extra monthly** on mortgage while both wages continue.
S0.quote: A café can be busy and still have the wrong stock value on its policy.
fieldNote: His **business-policy skill** spots stock changes that would distort a premium.
His **ten-month reserve** reflects current pay and two present wages, not guaranteed future income.

steps.text: Review disputed small-business renewals every Friday against signed declarations
Pay 100 extra toward mortgage monthly while both wages continue

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say Steady Disruption may write renewal letters and check business declarations before a clerk opens them. I want the insurer to show error rates and paid human review hours before setting new targets.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My lead hours could shrink if one clerk manages several automated renewal queues. Our ten-month reserve helps, but Hana’s current school-office wage alone would not cover our mortgage and all basic bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask my manager this month for a paid demonstration of the new renewal checker on invented café files, with our present hours protected. If approved I would learn its limits and bring missed stock changes to the workplace group; if my hours fall I would check actual local policy posts with enough net pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my own hours and curious about whether the tool catches real changes. An impressive screen cannot pay the mortgage if the team loses shifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the workplace group request?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The group would ask for written paid review hours and a person who signs off wrong premiums. I would bring examples, not claim the manager has agreed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What makes a nearby job real?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would need a posted salary, hours and net pay that cover our share of the household budget. A nearby office with no vacancy is not an option.

say: I would demand **paid human review** and visible error rates.
I would test **invented café files** with protected current hours.
think: I could lose **lead hours** when queues combine.
I cannot replace **my wage** with Hana’s current pay alone.
do: **Request paid tool demonstration** this month with protected hours.
**Learn renewal checker limits** if approved and bring errors to workplace group.
**Check posted local jobs** if hours fall and net pay covers household bills.
S1.quote: An impressive screen cannot pay the mortgage if the team loses shifts.
fieldNote: His **new tool learning** is conditional on paid time and protected current hours.
The **group request** needs approval, while the job search needs actual posted work covering household bills.

steps.text: Learn new renewal checker in paid demonstration if approved with current hours protected
Bring missed stock changes to workplace group for paid review hours if approved
Check posted local policy jobs if hours fall and net pay covers bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the renewal team that AGI by 2028 could read declarations, price policies and answer owners more cheaply than us. Robots visiting business premises might follow around 2031, but our desk work would change first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my lead renewal job to end, and I have been awake at night running the mortgage numbers. Ten months saved buys search time, but Hana’s school-office wage alone cannot carry the whole household.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would request written notice of cuts now and stop the extra mortgage payment if my hours fall, keeping cash for monthly bills. If my job ends in the first year after 2028, I would apply only to actual local paid customer claims posts with enough net income, and I would ask the employment office what support I qualify for.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed about losing the larger wage. Ten months is a cushion, not ten months of new pay arriving.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could customer claims survive?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Customer claims work may also be automated, so I would read the contract length and duties before accepting. I would not tell Hana we are safe because an advertisement uses a friendly job title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would public support pay the mortgage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would use the support office only after it confirms our eligibility. I will not budget an allowance that has not been approved.

say: I would warn **renewal desk work** faces AGI by 2028.
I would put **premises robots later**, around 2031.
think: I expect my **lead wage to end** and lose sleep over mortgage figures.
I know **Hana’s present wage** cannot cover our full bills.
do: **Request written cut notice** and preserve mortgage cash now.
**Apply after 2028 loss** only to real paid local posts covering household bills.
**Ask support office** about actual eligibility if displaced.
feel: **Alarmed** and losing sleep over expected major wage loss.
S2.quote: Ten months is a cushion, not ten months of new pay arriving.
fieldNote: He expects **major wage loss** and describes broken sleep despite the strong reserve.
A **claims opening or allowance** needs real paid work or confirmed eligibility.

steps.text: Request written cut notice and stop extra mortgage payment if hours fall
Apply to real paid local claims roles after 2028 loss if net pay covers bills
Ask employment office about support eligibility if displaced

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say AGI by 2031 gives us five years to find paid apprenticeships before renewal work changes completely. Robots doing physical site work may follow around 2034, so a trade is a bridge, not a promise for life.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have helped my uncle fix wiring but I am not a qualified electrician. I would only consider a formal apprenticeship if the paid trainee rate plus Hana’s current wage covers our mortgage and bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would call two registered electrical firms for actual paid apprentice openings and ask about safety training, licence rules and take-home pay. If a registered supervised offer protects my current paid renewal shifts in writing, I would enrol only if household take-home pay after commuting and required tools or fees still covers the mortgage and basic bills; after 2031 loss I would take a qualified paid place only if it exists and passes that same budget.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing the desk wage but can measure a five-year route. A toolbox from my uncle is not an electrician’s licence.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a real apprenticeship include?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask who signs the training hours and what protective gear the firm supplies. If the offer is unpaid or clashes with current shifts, I would keep my insurance job and save.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would trade work last?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Around 2034 robots might take some physical tasks too. I would ask the firm which paid electrical work remains before betting our mortgage on it.

say: I would seek **paid registered apprenticeship** with safety training.
I would name **2034 robots** as a later trade risk.
think: I am **not qualified** from family repair experience.
I need **net household pay** after commute, required tools and fees to cover mortgage and bills.
do: **Call two registered firms** for paid openings, licence rules and net pay.
Enrol only with **protected paid shifts** and household pay after commute, tools and fees covering mortgage and bills.
**Take qualified paid place** after 2031 loss only if net pay after work costs covers bills.
feel: **Anxious** about later wage loss, with a measured training option.
S3.quote: A toolbox from my uncle is not an electrician’s licence.
fieldNote: His **trade route** requires real paid apprenticeship, safety training, shift fit and household bill coverage.
He treats **physical robots** after 2031 as a later risk, not a permanent escape.

steps.text: Call two registered firms about paid electrical apprenticeships and safety requirements
Enrol supervised only with protected shifts and pay after commute tools fees covering bills
Take qualified paid electrical post after 2031 loss if available and pay after costs covers bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues AGI by 2036 offers a decade to pay down debt and see which paid skills still matter. Robots doing site work might follow around 2039, after the policy desk changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our work and mortgage feel secure for the next few years, though I am 27 and need more than this title for a lifetime. I would keep the debt falling without assuming Hana’s future wages stay the same.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep Friday renewal checks and put an extra 150 toward the mortgage monthly while both present wages hold. Once a year I would ask registered trade firms for actual paid trainee rates; after 2036 loss I would move only to an actual qualified paid post if household take-home pay after commuting and required tools or fees still covers the mortgage and basic bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the distant desk risk, but we can pay our bills now. A smaller loan would make a lower trainee wage less frightening.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you test the trainee wage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would subtract commuting and required tools or fees from trainee pay, then compare household take-home income with our mortgage and bills. If the maths fails, I would wait and keep the insurance wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Can Hana promise future support?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not ask Hana to promise to carry us in 2036. We can only plan from the earnings we see and revise the budget each year.

I would keep **business renewals checked** before AGI in 2036.

do: **Check business renewals** every Friday while current work pays.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because I expect my larger renewal wage to go before I can qualify for a paid trade. Written notice, a real bill-covering job and a registered paid apprenticeship would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask what an apprentice actually takes home after travel and tools. I would put the trainee pay beside our mortgage statement before signing an apprenticeship contract.

headlineQuote: I would put the trainee pay beside our mortgage statement before signing an apprenticeship contract.
portrait: Zane is a **27-year-old renewal lead** with a bachelor’s degree and above-typical pay.
He and Hana **pay a mortgage**, have no children and hold ten months of expenses.
He uses **AI occasionally** for letters and checks shop stock against signed policy terms.
He considers **registered paid electrical training** only with safety rules, real openings and household bill coverage.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end his larger renewal wage before he qualifies for a paid trade.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, bill-covering paid work and a registered paid apprenticeship would help.
